text: All parties have repaired their facilities, maintained supplies for six consecutive rounds, stocked raw materials, and resumed trade. Postwar monitoring has ended, with a 1800-second transitional ceasefire in effect. Casualties and old debts remain part of history.
Postwar arrangements have been recorded. Ongoing supply and treaty obligations must still be fulfilled each round.
Conditions have changed. This action was not carried out.

When the guns fall silent, the ruins still need clearing, interrupted supplies must be restored, and wartime alliances must be honored. Each party must weigh its own interests at the postwar conference. Every step, from ceasefire monitoring to repairing production lines and reopening workshops, comes at a real cost.

Each party independently weighs the costs and benefits. Upon agreeing, each contributes 30 food/4 parts/20 knowledge. Once the ceasefire takes effect, each contributes 6 food/1 part/2 knowledge every 300 seconds to maintain monitoring. It is void if supplies are missed for three consecutive rounds, and can last no longer than 6000 seconds. The settlement is complete only after all parties' facilities are fully repaired, services are stable, raw material reserves cover at least three rounds, and no payments are overdue, all continuously for six rounds, and at least two postwar shipments have arrived in port and been delivered.
